drugClass.name: hepatitis B virus (HBV) mRNA-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO)

provenance.quote: HIBSAGO is a hepatitis B virus (HBV) mRNA-directed antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) indicated

paragraphs: HIBSAGO is a prescription medicine used with other medicines called nucleos(t)ide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NrtIs), to treat adults with chronic (long-term) hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection without advanced liver disease (cirrhosis):
who have been on NrtI treatment for at least 6 months and have undetectable HBV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and
who have low levels of HBV surface antigen (HBsAg less than or equal to 3,000 IU/mL) Your healthcare provider will perform tests to make sure HIBSAGO is right for you.

sections.title: Mechanism of Action
sections.text: HIBSAGO is an antiviral drug against HBV [see Microbiology (12.4)] .

sections.title: Pharmacodynamics
sections.text: Exposure Response Within the range of bepirovirsen exposures achieved at the dosing regimen in B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 trials, variability in bepirovirsen plasma exposure was not identified as a determinant of treatment response at Week 72. Immunostimulant Activity In nonclinical studies, bepirovirsen exhibited innate immune activity in a sequence-specific, human toll-like receptor 8 (hTLR8)-dependent manner, with no activity observed at other pattern recognition receptors tested. This was demonstrated in an hTLR8-overexpressing cell line and confirmed in transgenic hTLR8 knock-in mice. Compared to wild-type mice, hTLR8 knock-in mice showed increased proinflammatory cytokine expression upon bepirovirsen treatment. This immunostimulatory activity was predominantly localized to hepatic macrophages and Kupffer cells, with induction of cytokines including TNF- α, IL -12p40, and CXCL10. In clinical studies, administration of HIBSAGO was associated with increases in innate immune markers of activation and trafficking, which included cytokines and chemokines (e.g., interleukin12, tumor necrosis factor, interferon gamma and CXC motif chemokine ligand 9 and 10). Treatment with HIBSAGO also increased total IgM. In addition, treatment with HIBSAGO led to immunophenotypic changes in peripheral B and T cells (including increases in Ki67 positive B and T cells and increases in granzyme B positive cluster of differentiation 8, T cell frequencies). The contribution of immunostimulatory activity to antiviral activity at therapeutic concentrations in humans has not been fully determined. Cardiac Electrophysiology At supratherapeutic doses of 450 or 600 mg (1.5 and 2 times the recommended dosage) of HIBSAGO, clinically significant QTc interval prolongation was not observed.

sections.title: Pharmacokinetics
sections.text: The pharmacokinetic parameters of bepirovirsen 300 mg are summarized in Table 7. Table 7. Pharmacokinetic Properties of Bepirovirsen General Information Exposure C max (mcg/mL) a 9.14 (2.19) AUC 0-tau (mcg*hour/mL) a 102 (34.3) C trough (mcg/mL) a 0.022 (0.045) Dose proportionality Exposure increased in proportion to dose over the range of 150 to 300 mg weekly dosing Time to steady state Steady state concentration is reached by Day 8 following 300 mg weekly dosing with loading doses during Weeks 1 and 2 Accumulation No accumulation was observed with 300 mg weekly dosing for 24 weeks Absorption T max , (hours) b 3 (2-5) Distribution V ss /F (L) c 73 (46.3) Plasma Protein Binding 99% at 5 mcg/mL 95% at 150 mcg/mL Elimination Major route of elimination Metabolism Terminal Half-life (days) b 29 (8-192) Clearance/F (L/hour) c 3.05 (25.7) Metabolism Primary Pathway Metabolized in tissues by endonucleases to form shorter oligonucleotides that are then substrates for additional metabolism by exonucleases Excretion Urine Oligonucleotide fragments are expected to be excreted by the kidney C max = maximum plasma concentration; AUC 0-tau = area under the time concentration curve from 0 to dosing interval; T max = time to peak concentration; Vss = Volume of Distribution at steady-state. a Pharmacokinetic parameters are presented as arithmetic mean (SD), derived from population PK model simulations at steady state following subcutaneous administration of HIBSAGO 300 mg weekly in participants with chronic HBV infection (CHB). b observed median (min-max) c Pharmacokinetic parameters are presented as geometric mean (CV%) from post-hoc individual estimates from Phase 3 population PK model. Specific Populations Based on population pharmacokinetic analyses, following subcutaneous administration, there were no clinically meaningful changes in the pharmacokinetics of bepirovirsen by race (Asian, Black, White, Other), ethnicity, age (18-87 years old), sex, body weight (39 kg to 148 kg), injection site location (thigh, upper arm, abdomen) and anti-drug antibodies (ADA) status. Renal Impairment: Bepirovirsen pharmacokinetics were similar between patients with CHB with an eGFR 60 to 89 mL/min/1.73m 2 compared to patients with an eGFR ≥90 mL/min/1.73 m 2 . Insufficient data are available in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment. Hepatic Impairment: The pharmacokinetics of bepirovirsen have not been evaluated in CHB patients with hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A, B, or C) [see Contraindications (4)] . There is a 33% reduction in C max and a 31% reduction in AUC 0- ∞ in participants with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class B) but without HBV infection when compared to participants with normal hepatic function. Drug Interaction Studies No formal clinical drug interaction studies have been conducted with HIBSAGO. In clinical trials, concomitant administration of HIBSAGO with a NrtI did not result in changes in bepirovirsen exposure. In addition, HIBSAGO did not impact NrtI exposure. Based on in vitro study results, HIBSAGO is not a substrate, inducer or inhibitor of major cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes, or drug transporters; therefore, clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions are not expected.

definition.text: INFLAMMATION of the LIVER in humans caused by HEPATITIS B VIRUS lasting six months or more. It is primarily transmitted by parenteral exposure, such as transfusion of contaminated blood or blood products, but can also be transmitted via sexual or intimate personal contact.

definition.text: INFLAMMATION of the LIVER with ongoing hepatocellular injury for 6 months or more, characterized by NECROSIS of HEPATOCYTES and inflammatory cell (LEUKOCYTES) infiltration. Chronic hepatitis can be caused by viruses, medications, autoimmune diseases, and other unknown factors.

arms.label: Not-on-NA participants
arms.description: Participants rolling over from study 209668 who have not received nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy during the parent study and remain off NAs will be included in this arm. Participants will be followed up for 33 months. Participants maintaining either functional cure (FC) or a partial response off NA treatment at Month 33 will be eligible to be followed up for an additional 2 years. No study treatment will be administered in this study.

arms.label: On-NA participants
arms.description: Participants rolling over from studies 209668, 209348, 212602, 202009, 219288, and 217023 who entered the parent study on stable NA therapy and remained on NA therapy for the duration of the treatment and follow-up periods in the parent study will be included in this arm. NA cessation will occur at 3 months in 206882 for eligible and willing participants. Participants will be followed up for 33 months. Participants rolling over from studies 209668 and 209348 who stopped NA treatment and are maintaining either FC or a partial response at Month 33, and remaining off NA treatment, will be eligible to be followed up for an additional 2 years. No study treatment will be administered in this study.

arms.label: NA-cessated participants
arms.description: Participants rolling over from studies 202009 and 219288 who have stopped NA treatment during the parent study will be included in this arm. Participants will be followed up for 33 months. No study treatment will be administered in this study.
